text.content: Meridian's operations manager has requested a new capability, a weekly engagement briefing that loops through a list of active client accounts and produces a one-line status summary for each one. Rather than a consultant querying each account manually one at a time, the agent should process the entire list in a single execution and return all summaries together.

text.content: This is a fundamentally different pattern from what has been built so far. The existing canvas handles one query at a time. Processing a collection of items requires a different node. This is known as the Iteration Node.

text.content: The Iteration Node executes a defined sub-flow (a sequence of nodes nested within it) for each item in an input array, implementing a for-each loop. For every individual element within that array, the Iteration Node sequentially executes the sequence of nodes visually placed inside its boundaries on the canvas.

text.content: The Iteration Node handles collection processing that would otherwise require multiple manual queries or a custom scripted loop. The key design principle is that nodes inside the Iteration Node boundary execute per item while nodes outside execute once after all items are processed. Understanding this boundary is what makes the difference between a flow that processes a list correctly and one that processes only the first item or collapses all items into a single pass.
